en: Points of Controversy,
Great Chapter Fifteen,
Sixteenth Section.
Discourse on the Inclusion within the Form and Formless Realms:
Is lust for the form realm included within the form realm? Yes.

Is it associated with, co-arisen with, conjoined with, and connected to the mind that is desirable for attainment, the mind that is desirable for rebirth, and the mind that is a pleasant abiding in this very life;
and does it have the same arising, the same cessation, the same basis, and the same object as those minds?
It should not be said so... [as before] ...

Is it not the case that it is neither desirable as an attainment (*samāpatti*), nor desirable as a rebirth (*upapatti*), nor a pleasant dwelling in this very life (*diṭṭhadhammasukhavihāra*), and that it has a mind which is not desirable as an attainment... [as before] ...and that it has the same basis and the same object?
Yes, it is so.

If it is not to be attained through meditative absorption, not to be attained through rebirth, and not a pleasant abiding in this very life; and if it is not by means of a mind to be attained through absorption … [as before] … having the same basis and the same object, then indeed, sir, you should not say:
“Lust for the form realm is included within the form realm.
Is lust for the form realm included within the form realm?
“Yes.
“Is desire for sounds included within the sound-element?
One should not say so … [and so on] …
Is lust for form included within the form realm?
Yes. Is lust for fragrance … [and so on] … included within the form realm? Yes.
Is attachment to tastes …pe… attachment to tangibles included within the element of tangibles?
It should not be said so …pe….
Is it not to be said of sound-desire that it is "included within the sound-element"?
Yes, it is.
Should it not be said that attachment to form is "included within the realm of form"?
It should not be so stated... [and so forth].
Scent-desire … [and so on] … taste-desire … [and so on] … touch-desire should not be said to be—
“Is it included within the tangible-element?
Yes. “Should it be said that lust for form is [included within the tangible-element]? No.
“Is it included within the form realm?
One should not say so… [and so on]… Is attachment to the formless included within the formless realm?
“Yes,” he said.
“Is it not to be said that attachment to the formless (arūparāga) is included within the formless realm (arūpadhātu)?”
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Is attachment to the formless included within the formless realm? Yes.

Is it associated with, co-arisen with, conjoined with, and associated with the mind that leads to attainment, the mind that leads to rebirth, and the mind that dwells in happiness in the present life;
and is it of one arising, one cessation, one basis, and one object?

It should not be said so … [as before] … Is it not the case that it is neither desirable as an attainment, nor desirable as a rebirth, nor a pleasant abiding in this very life; and that it has a mind that is not desirable as an attainment … [as before] … and that it has the same basis and the same object?
Yes, it is.
If it were not to be attained through meditative absorption, nor to be attained through rebirth, nor a pleasant dwelling in this very life;

and if it were not accompanied by, co-arisen with, conjoined with, associated with, of a single arising, a single cessation, a single basis, and a single object with the mind that is to be attained through absorption, the mind that is to be attained through rebirth, or the mind that is a pleasant dwelling in this very life—then indeed, you should not say: [that it exists].
“Lust for the formless is included within the formless realm.
Is lust for the formless included within the formless realm? Yes.
Is sensual lust included within the sense-sphere element?
One should not say so … [and so on] … Is formless lust included within the formless-element?
“Yes.
“Sensual lust for odors … sensual lust for tastes …” [and so forth].
Is lust for the tangible included within the element of the tangible?
One should not say so … [and so on] … Lust for sound should not be said [to be included within the element of sound].
“Is it included within the element of faith?
Yes. It should not be said that formless lust is [included within the element of faith].
“Is it included within the formless realm?
One should not say so … [and so on] … [regarding] lust for odors … [and so on].
Is attachment to tastes … pe … attachment to tangibles not to be described as "included within the tangible element"?
“Yes.
Is it not to be said that attachment to the formless (arūparāga) is included within the formless realm (arūpadhātu)?
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Should it not be said:
“Sensual desire for the form realm is included within the form realm; sensual desire for the formless realm is included within the formless realm”?
“Yes.
“Is it not the case that sensual lust is included within the sense-sphere realm?
“Yes.”

If sensual lust is included within the sense-sphere realm (kāmadhātu), then indeed it must be said that "lust for the fine-material realm is included within the fine-material realm (rūpadhātu), and lust for the immaterial realm is included within the immaterial realm (arūpadhātu).
Lust for the fine-material realm is included within the fine-material realm; [and so is] lust for the immaterial realm...
The discussion on whether [the mind] is included within the formless realm is finished.
This is the sixteenth chapter. Its summary verse (uddāna) is as follows:
Restraint of the mind, exertion of the mind, the bestowing of happiness, attention having attained [the object], matter as cause, matter with cause,
matter that is both wholesome and unwholesome, matter that is result, there is matter belonging to the fine-material sphere and there is matter belonging to the immaterial sphere,
and all defilements are included within the sense-sphere.
